clue.text: Mountains which provide mice

parts.note: split the range's name into two words and it describes what felines do to rodents, so the hills seem to supply the dead prey

explanation.surface: A range of hills somehow serves as a source of rodents.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the name as a sentence, CATS KILL, and it says what happens to mice. The Catskills are a mountain range in New York State.
explanation.definitionFit: The Catskill range is a group of peaks in New York State, and the cryptic reading turns its name into a statement about cats and their prey.

clue.text: The winners have tea with members

parts.note: cha is an old slang word for tea
MPs are Members of Parliament

explanation.surface: The victorious side relax over a cuppa with parliamentarians.
explanation.definitionFit: Champs is informal shorthand for champions, those who have won.

clue.text: Qualities which are reverse of one in origin

indicators.note: the phrase tells us to read the whole built-up word from back to front
one piece is put inside the other, as the clue says one is in the origin

parts.note: a start is a beginning or origin
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Characteristics that turn out to be the opposite of a single source.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts I inside START to give STIART, and 'reverse of' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: Traits are distinguishing features or characteristics of a person.

clue.text: Something instrumental for a vital committee

parts.note: key means crucial or vital
a board is a governing committee

explanation.surface: Something that proves useful to an important panel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Something instrumental' looks like 'useful', but it means a set of keys on a musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A keyboard is the row of keys on a piano or organ, a part of a musical instrument.

clue.text: Sexy glance at a rising dance

indicators.note: in a down entry the word climbs, so it is read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: a reel is a lively Scottish dance

explanation.surface: Someone casts a suggestive look at a dancer getting up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns REEL so it reads upwards in this down light. A reel is a lively Scottish folk dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A leer is a lustful or suggestive sidelong look.

clue.text: Body with an extra note in its heart

indicators.note: signals that one piece sits inside the other, as the note sits in the heart

parts.note: the core of something is its heart or centre
PS (postscript) is a note added at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: A body with an added message tucked into its centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts PS inside CORE. 'Body' here means a dead one.
explanation.definitionFit: A corpse is a dead body.

clue.text: Orchestral player with wood at heart

definitions.text: Orchestral player with wood at heart

parts.words: Orchestral player with wood at heart
parts.note: a musician whose instrument belongs to the woodwind section, so wood lies at the centre of what this player does

explanation.surface: A musician in an orchestra is a woodland lover at heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wood at heart' sounds like a love of trees, but it points to the woodwind section where this player sits.
explanation.definitionFit: An oboist plays the oboe, a double-reed woodwind instrument in the orchestra.

clue.text: Children give father attitudes about love

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father

indicators.note: signals that one piece goes around another, the poses being wrapped about the love

parts.note: poses are bodily attitudes or postures
O is love, a zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: Kids make their dad strike affectionate postures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts O inside POSES to make POOSES, after PA.
explanation.definitionFit: Papooses are young Native American babies, so infants or little ones.

clue.text: Hand-picked boy is a constituent of atoms

parts.note: elect means chosen or selected
Ron is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A specially selected lad turns out to be a basic particle.
explanation.definitionFit: An electron is a negatively charged subatomic particle found in every atom.

clue.text: Separates into component parts as sanely as possible

indicators.note: what is possible could take another form, so these letters are rearranged into a different order

explanation.surface: Someone breaks a problem down as rationally as they can.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possible' rearranges SANELY AS. The first 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To analyse something is to examine it by breaking it into its elements.

clue.text: King holds up a pair

indicators.note: one piece holds another inside it, so the second word goes within the first

parts.note: Old King Cole is the merry monarch of the nursery rhyme
taken as written

explanation.surface: A monarch lifts two things high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds' puts UP inside COLE. King Cole is the merry old soul of a nursery rhyme.
explanation.definitionFit: A couple is two of something, a twosome.

clue.text: An aid for the lame may make one care about insolence

indicators.note: about can mean around in disorder, so these letters are turned about and rearranged

parts.note: lip is cheeky talk or insolence

explanation.surface: A walking support might make someone mind rudeness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges CARE with LIP. 'may make one' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A caliper is a metal leg brace that supports a weak or injured limb.

clue.text: Protector of two men

parts.note: Pat is a man's name
Ron is another man's name

explanation.surface: A guardian belonging to a pair of fellows.
explanation.definitionFit: A patron is a supporter or champion, like a patron saint who guards.

clue.text: Permit to provide one with a drink

parts.note: to pass is to hand over or provide
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: Permission to give someone a fortified wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Permit' is a noun here, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A passport is an official document allowing its holder to travel.

clue.text: Without two parties treatment would be fashionable evil

parts.note: in means fashionable

indicators.note: taking these letters out leaves the other phrase, so they belong within it

parts.note: sin is wickedness or evil
U (Unionist) and L (Liberal) are abbreviations for political parties

explanation.surface: Remove two political groups and therapy becomes trendy wickedness.
explanation.walkthrough: Take UL (Unionist and Liberal) out of the answer and IN SIN is left; so UL goes inside. 'would be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Insulin is the hormone given to diabetics as medical therapy.

clue.text: The man is after money

indicators.note: one piece follows the other, so the second word is written behind the first

parts.note: the franc was French currency

explanation.surface: A fellow is chasing cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts IS behind FRANC. 'The man' is a vague definition of a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Francis is a man's first name, so it can stand for a particular man.

clue.text: Woman's love for a brave man

parts.note: her is the possessive for a woman
O is love, nil in tennis

explanation.surface: A woman's passion for a courageous fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: A hero is someone admired for courage.

clue.text: Helped performers in favour of Heath

parts.note: pro means for or in favour of
Edward (Ted) Heath, British Prime Minister in the 1970s, was a long-serving MP

explanation.surface: Supporting a politician helped the actors.
explanation.walkthrough: Heath is MP TED: Ted Heath was a Conservative Prime Minister and a long-serving Member of Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: To prompt actors is to feed them forgotten lines from the wings.

clue.text: Woman canes deviant patron

parts.note: Mae is a woman's name

indicators.note: deviant means straying from the norm, so these letters stray into a new order

explanation.surface: A woman beats a wayward sponsor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deviant' rearranges CANES after MAE.
explanation.definitionFit: Maecenas was a wealthy Roman who backed Virgil and Horace; his name stands for any generous arts sponsor.

clue.text: Neat Tory turns out to be one legally empowered

indicators.note: the letters are turned out of their order and come out rearranged

explanation.surface: A tidy Conservative proves to be a lawyer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns out' rearranges NEAT TORY. A Tory is a British Conservative.
explanation.definitionFit: An attorney is someone with legal authority to act for another.

clue.text: Alternative backing with time to wander

indicators.note: going backwards, so the word is read from the end to the start

parts.note: or introduces an alternative
a.m. is a time of the morning

explanation.surface: Another option goes into reverse with some leisure for strolling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns OR round to RO.
explanation.definitionFit: To roam is to wander aimlessly.

clue.text: Catch in an instrument shaped like a crescent

definitions.note: describes a thing; the answer is the crescent-shaped thing itself

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other, the catch going in the instrument

parts.note: a lute is a stringed instrument
to net is to catch

explanation.surface: A trap inside a curved musical device.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts NET inside LUTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A lunette is a half-moon-shaped object or space, such as a semicircular window.

clue.text: White man gives father a variety of hake

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father

indicators.note: a variety is a different form, so these letters take a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A European offers his dad an assortment of fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a variety of' rearranges HAKE after PA.
explanation.definitionFit: Pakeha is the Maori word for a New Zealander of European descent.

clue.text: If it is not spotted all the rest are

definitions.text: If it is not spotted all the rest are

parts.words: If it is not spotted all the rest are
parts.note: the tiles in this game carry spots, all except the plain blank, which shares its name with the whole set

explanation.surface: A riddle about one plain thing among many dotted ones.
explanation.walkthrough: The game's tiles are marked with spots; the blank is the only one that is not.
explanation.definitionFit: A domino is a small tile marked with pips, the spots used in the game.

clue.text: An ear for a story on myself

indicators.note: in a down entry one piece sits on top of the next, so it comes first

parts.note: me stands for oneself
a lie is a made-up story

explanation.surface: A listener for a tale about oneself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' sets ME above A LIE in this down light. 'ear' means an ear of corn.
explanation.definitionFit: Mealie is the South African word for maize, especially a cob of it.

clue.text: It sounds as if a shoe seems to laugh at a vice

indicators.note: tells us the answer is pronounced like the words that follow

parts.note: to mock a sin is to laugh at a vice

explanation.surface: Footwear apparently ridicules wrongdoing.
explanation.walkthrough: MOCK A SIN said aloud gives the answer. 'seems to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A moccasin is a soft leather slipper, originally worn by Native Americans.

clue.text: Gloomy when half moon appeared above horizon

indicators.note: only half of the word is wanted, its first two letters

parts.note: the sun or moon rose when it came up over the horizon

explanation.surface: Sombre as a partial moon came up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' keeps MO, the first part of MOON.
explanation.definitionFit: Morose means sullen and melancholy.

clue.text: Game for an aircraft manoeuvre on taking off

indicators.note: a plane taking off climbs, so in this down light the word reads upwards

parts.note: a loop is a stunt in which a plane flies in a vertical circle

explanation.surface: A pastime for a stunt plane as it leaves the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on taking off' turns LOOP to read upwards. Pool is a cue game.
explanation.definitionFit: Pool is a cue game played on a table with pockets.

clue.text: Coloured egg rejected — it readily ignites

indicators.note: a rejected word is sent back, so the whole combination is reversed

parts.note: red means coloured, as in flushed
a nit is the egg of a louse

explanation.surface: A dyed egg is thrown out, as it catches fire easily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns round REDNIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinder is dry kindling material that catches fire easily.

clue.text: Magazine which is a pile of cereal

parts.note: corn is a cereal crop
a hill is a heap or pile

explanation.surface: A periodical that is just a heap of grain.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cornhill was a famous Victorian literary magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cornhill Magazine was a London literary periodical founded in 1860.

clue.text: Consternation is a theory in time

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other, the theory going in the time

parts.note: a day is a period of time
an ism is a doctrine or theory

explanation.surface: Alarm is an idea in its era.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts ISM inside DAY. The first 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Dismay is alarm and distress.

clue.text: Sword laying Sir Thomas on the earth

indicators.note: one piece is set on the other, so it comes after it in this across entry

parts.note: clay is earth or soil
Sir Thomas More was a Tudor statesman and author of Utopia

explanation.surface: Someone lays a famous Tudor statesman on the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' puts MORE after CLAY. A claymore is a Scottish broadsword.
explanation.definitionFit: A claymore is a large two-edged Scottish broadsword.
